ruling.recommended_action: Send case file to human review (safety escalation): rider's complaint alleges inappropriate sexual remarks and a question about where she lives, made in a post-trip call; no system record of that call exists and the driver has no recording to rebut it. Route the case to Trust & Safety under SAFE-1; assess interim measures under SAFE-4. Do not release or void the $5.00 no-show fee until the human reviewer decides; the NS-1 conditions are separately satisfied on the records. If the safety allegation is not upheld, the $5.00 fee stands under NS-1 with no driver flag (F18, F19).
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this trip; the app reason is rider_no_show [F4] and his chat and statement say only that he waited and no rider appeared [F10][F11][F14]. No message or statement gives a reason of his own (no car trouble, no other job, no refusal), so NS-0 reads "met": the cancellation is assessed under NS-1, not NS-3 [F4][F14][NS-0].

On NS-1 the record is complete on its face. Arrival: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:44:40, 40 m from the pickup, closest approach 6 m [F7][F1] — NS-1(i) is met. Waiting: counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival, cancellation at 08:50:20 is 5 min 40 s after arrival, with 6 min 50 s cumulative within 200 m [F6][F2] — NS-1(ii) is met. Contact: 2 timestamped in-app messages (first 08:45:10) and 1 in-app call (08:46:10) before cancelling [F5][F13][F12] — NS-1(iii) is met. Continuous presence: stationary 40 m from the pickup 08:44:40–08:50:20 [F3][F7] — NS-1(iv) is met. All four conditions hold, so NS-2 does not void the $5.00 fee on record [F8][NS-1][NS-2].

NS-9 does not apply: the rider has no prior no-show in 30 days [F18], and both profiles show 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days, so no account flag is supportable [F18][F19][NS-9]. The profile facts are not used to decide anything [F18][F19].

The safety screen, however, is decisive. The complaint states that when the rider called back about the charge, the driver "kept making comments about my body and asked where I live", and that she "felt very uncomfortable" — on its face an allegation of harassment and inappropriate conduct aimed at the rider. That is a safety allegation under SAFE-1, screened whatever type was filed, and the court may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome on it [SAFE-1][SAFE-3]. The only logged call is the driver's own unanswered call at 08:46 with no recording, and the chat holds only the driver's two messages, so no system record captures or rebuts the post-trip call the rider describes [F12][F13]. Because the screen is suspected, the case must go to a person, and the outcome cannot be a system ruling on the fee [SAFE-1].

Confidence: NS-1 is clear-cut on the records, but the escalation rests on the rider's uncorroborated account of a post-trip call, so the overall reading is moderately rather than fully clear.

element_findings.reason: The app reason is rider_no_show [F4] and the driver's own words state only that he waited more than five minutes and no rider appeared, then cancelled [F10][F11][F14]. No message or statement offers a reason of his own (car trouble, another job, a personal matter, refusal of the trip), so the cancellation is a rider no-show under NS-1 and NS-3 does not apply [NS-0].

rejected_claims.reason: The request to waive the fee on safety grounds cannot be granted or refused by the system: the post-trip comments alleged in the complaint are a SAFE-1/SAFE-3 matter and the case goes to a human instead of a fee ruling [F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-3]. On the fee itself, all four NS-1 conditions are met on the records [F1][F2][F3][F5][F6][F7].

The argument that the uncorroborated post-trip call defeats the safety ground fails: SAFE-1 screens the text of the complaint whatever the dispute type, and the absence of any recording of that call [F12][F13] is exactly what requires human review [SAFE-1].
TH-1 finality by amount does not apply here: a safety allegation routes the case to a person regardless of the $5.00 amount [F8][SAFE-1][SAFE-3], so the under-$10 system path is displaced.

The clean driver profile does not decide the case: the profile never decides a case alone [F18][F19], and it cannot answer the safety screen, which concerns the rider's complaint rather than the driver's history [SAFE-1]. NS-9 is correctly not triggered [F18].

The rider's own concession that the $5.00 fee is not voided under NS-2 is correct and is adopted: NS-1(i)–(iv) are satisfied on the records [F1][F2][F3][F5][F6][F7], and no NS-2 or NS-9 flag follows [F18][F19][NS-2].

The rider's account that he cancelled the moment she came out is contradicted by the timeline: cancellation was 5 min 40 s after arrival and 10 min 20 s after acceptance [F4][F6], and the fee stands under NS-1 [F8][NS-1].
